parse_text: SILICERNIUM, among the Romanus was a fault of a private nature, provided for the Great line time after the funeral. It confited of beans, lettues, bread, eggs, &co. Their eyes laid upon the tomb, and they possibly believed that the died would come out of the repair. What was left was generally burnt on the floor. The word _Alternate_ as derived from _Place and_ crear, i. e. of figure upon a fleece . Eating what had thus been provided for the dead, was effecemed amark of the small minerible powder. A similar entertainment was made by the Greek sit in the tender of the seaside; but it was ufalal among them to treat the globils with the fragments from the feat of the living. See FUNFAL AND INTERLE.
